conf.description: crowdstrike-falcon, audit-activity dataset, syslog-leef format: split the LEEF 1.0 pipe-delimited header, tokenize the tab-delimited attribute body into the crowdstrike.falcon.* namespace by literal key, tag event.dataset. reveal_token/API-key masking recommended by the catalog is NOT implemented -- no concrete field or pattern given.

conf.comment: crowdstrike-falcon / audit-activity / syslog-leef (AuthActivityAuditEvent / UserActivityAuditEvent, same stream/connector as detection-summary). leef.cfg audit attribute keys are unpublished, so attributes land under crowdstrike.falcon.<literal-key> without an asserted ECS mapping. The catalog recommends masking reveal_token/API-key values before indexing but names no concrete field or pattern for this format -- per the brief's masking rule, that is left as a documented gap, not invented.

functions.description: record why attribute-level ECS mapping and masking are both left undone
split the LEEF:1.0|vendor|product|version|eventType| header from the tab-delimited attribute body

conf.code: var body = __e['attrs'] || ''; var parts = body.split(String.fromCharCode(9)); for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { var eq = parts[i].indexOf('='); if (eq > 0) { var k = parts[i].substring(0, eq).trim(); var v = parts[i].substring(eq + 1); if (k.length > 0) { __e['crowdstrike.falcon.' + k] = v; } } }

functions.description: tokenize the tab-delimited LEEF attribute body into crowdstrike.falcon.<literal-key>
batch-rename the LEEF header capture groups into the custom namespace
tag the dataset and drop the working/raw fields now that every attribute has been extracted
